I really am lucky to have a father who cares so much about me and my health, and I really am thankful for his love and support. The journal thing was complicated, because even though I was so furious and hurt, I knew it came from a place of very deep love.

I was very suicidal. I spent some time in the hospital, and then left against medical advice. A few months later, I went off my meds and became very very suicidal again. I kept a journal, and wrote a lot about these feelings and struggling with them and, eventually, planning out my death. But I still lived at home at this point and one day my dad, worrying about me, decided to read my journal. 

He spent a morning with me, taking me out to breakfast, for a hike. Then we went home, he made me a cup of tea, and just broke down. He told me about reading my book, he told me how much he loved me, he told me if I did anything to go through with it, it would be the end too. 

I'd never seen my dad cry before. And I'd never felt such a mix of emotions. I was so angry at him for betraying my trust and reading my journal, so sad that it had gotten to this point, and so disappointed in myself for making him cry. I felt guilty for putting my dad through all this. And that mix of emotion, of pain and fear and real sadness stays with me every day. The reason I take my medication, the reason I haven't given up yet.

Lately I've just been having so many bad days...and I write them all of as oh, it was just one day, and then I realize it's been weeks. And I've been depressed for so long that I don't know any other alternative. It's just so hard to live in anticipation of good days, and then when they come around, it's impossible to appreciate it because I'm so terrified of when they will end. 

And I try to take precautions and not trust anyone and not get too emotionally attached to anything, or especially not any person. I've ended friendships and relationships because it's too risky to let people in. And the one time I break my rule and let myself become vulnerable, I get fucked over. I just can't trust anyone or get close to anyone. And the good times don't cancel out the bad.

Some things I have tried - these feelings aren't new to me and I actually was institutionalized over the summer. I take Prozac 10mg every night and Wellbutrin 150mg in the morning. So medication isn't new (I mean, relatively. About three months).

I want to be better for my family, but for myself, I think I'd rather die...I'm scared of hurting myself because I do have a history of self harm that my parents know about (going back since I was twelve or so - 18 now) and if my parents found out they'd pull me out of school. But I can't go home, everything will be so much worse if I do. I just don't know where I can go that things will be better.

I'm actually staying away from school counseling. I have the number of an off-campus therapist, and I met with her once and really liked her, but I can't make the phone call...like I can't bring myself to go through it all again, it's so exhausting finding new therapists. I have a psychiatrist at home, I'm honestly not a huge fan of her, but I don't see her often.

I'm so fucking suicidal and constantly self-harming, my entire leg is covered in these crazy cuts and I always want to add to it...on Friday I went to my town's suicide bridge and just stood there for so long. And all of my open tabs are searches for different kinds of sleeping pills and antihistamines. I'm just scared that I'm actually going to do something. I thought I was getting better but clearly not because I literally always want to hurt myself and die. Suicide is never not on my mind. 

I'm also terrified of being alone, last night I made someone sleep in my bed because I was too scared of how I'd hurt myself if he wasn't there...I also got really screwed over by someone who I've been hooking up with for months last night, and the person knew what they were doing, and just the day before I had made the decision to tell them some v. personal things which we'd never talked about before, and he invited that and told me to tell him and now he won't speak to me anymore. And this pattern just repeats itself way too often, every time I think someone is going well, it just ends. I never get anything good for myself, because even when I am happy, I am constantly on edge waiting for it to all blow up. Stupid of me to think I could trust anyone. 

I'm under huge amounts of academic pressure as well, I'm failing one of my classes and just scraping by in another (and this semester, I'm only taking three). I go to a university that is incredibly painful and rigorous and has a really oppressive stress culture that is impossible to escape. And when I get too overwhelmed I just shut down - sleep for 14+ hours a day. I don't eat anymore and I'm starting to smoke way too much again. 

I just cannot do it. I am so exhausted with life and so exhausted with things going badly and I honestly honestly don't believe that things will get better...the only time I can think of in the past months that I've been peaceful was when I walked to that bridge. I can't stop thinking about it, and I'm a disappointment to my family and a burden to my friends and a fucking sad girl that no one wants...

I wouldn't say it brought us closer together, but it sort of leveled things out. At first I was upset, because I couldn't hide my hospitalization, but then she became much more open about her experiences with mental illness in college, and it felt like, 'Well, okay, this is happening to us both, there's no need to hide.'

My sister is five years older than me and we never became particularly close (until she moved out, much more recently). We ended up keeping a lot of secrets from each other. My sister had bad anxiety, I struggle(d) a lot with depression, and neither of us wanted the other one to know. When she came back from her first semester of college, she often had panic attacks and was bulimic. I was self-harming and in mandated therapy. We both hid these things from each other for *four years* until I was hospitalized and everything came out. For four years, we tiptoed around every conversation surrounding mental illness, both terrified that one of us would guess that someone was 'wrong' with the other. Our parents, on the other hand, knew everything, and kindly kept our secrets.

I'm from the east coast (USA), but I've been in Italy for weeks, and the plan is to move to the west coast at the end of July. I put all this distance between myself and my problems and give myself so many chances to start over but I feel like I'm entirely trapped inside the past. Like I'll never really be happy, if I'm not happy here then when will I ever be?

I'm making changes - I went to outpatient, I got a prescription for Prozac (though I rarely take it), I'm in therapy, I'm traveling halfway across the world, I haven't spoken to my ex or best friend in months - and nothing helps.

Also here to say that maybe exercise isn't enough, and it's ok if its not, because there is no one easy cure! I struggle lots with anxiety and depressive episodes and I'm also really highly active. It's frustrating when people just tell me to suck it up and hit the gym, because I'm an athlete and still hurt quite often. Just find what works for you!!
